title: Filtered pages and their image abutment descend through filtered localization
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathcal H_f(R)$, $W$ be the uniformly finite filtered module homotopy category and its graded quasi-isomorphisms [def-kun-finite-filtered-module-homotopy]. Put $\mathcal D_f(R)=\mathcal H_f(R)[W^{-1}]$. Use cochain cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], successive filtration quotients [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] and the normalized page functor $S$ supplied by [lem-kun-filtered-page-functor-normalized] (refining [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core]), with the canonical map $\varphi(U,a,t):F^aU/F^{a+t}U\to F^{a-t+1}U/F^{a+1}U$ sending the class of $x$ to its class, for $t\ge1$. Write
$$I^a_n(U)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(F^aU)\to H^n(U)\bigr).$$
The functor $S$, together with the cohomology modules $H^n(U)$ equipped with $I_n$, factors through $\mathcal D_f(R)$. Specifically, filtered homotopic chain maps give equal maps on every page $t\ge1$, on cohomology and on $I^a_n$ and its successive quotients. Every $w\in W$ induces quasi-isomorphisms on every filtration-step complex and on the underlying complex, and induces isomorphisms on all pages $t\ge1$, on $H^n(U)$ and on each $I^a_n$ and its successive quotient. The descended map on $H^n$ is the ordinary cohomology map of the underlying derived morphism, and the page-one comparison is natural with component $H^{a+b}(\operatorname{gr}^a f)$.
For every $a,n$ and sufficiently large $t$, the image comparison of $S$ gives canonical isomorphisms
$$S(U)_t^{a,n-a}\cong\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(F^aU)\to H^n(U/F^{a+1}U)\bigr)\cong I^a_n(U)/I^{a+1}_n(U).$$
These are natural for all morphisms of $\mathcal D_f(R)$ once $t$ is sufficiently large for both objects. They agree on adjacent stationary pages under the normalized successor-page homology isomorphisms supplied by [lem-kun-filtered-page-functor-normalized]. The second displayed isomorphism is normalized by sending a class represented by a cycle $x\in F^aU^n$ to its cohomology class modulo $I^{a+1}_n(U)$; its inverse sends such a class to the class of $x$ in the image in $H^n(U/F^{a+1}U)$. No cochain-degree bound is imposed.

Localization extension uses Derived Categories Tags 05S1/05S2.

proof.text: Use the normalized quotient-page realization supplied by [lem-kun-filtered-page-functor-normalized], which retains the core page-one, image and representative clauses and fixes the successor isomorphisms. The supplied $\varphi$ exists because $F^{a+t}U\subseteq F^{a+1}U$ and $F^aU\subseteq F^{a-t+1}U$. Thus both projections kill the same required relations, and the quotient equation determines $\varphi$ uniquely. The normalized successor map sends a successor-cycle class to the same representative on page $t+1$; this is the canonical choice in the specified quotient construction, rather than an arbitrary isomorphic replacement.

source.place: Tag 012K (section-filtered-complex), Tag 012M (lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex), explicit cycle/boundary construction and successor quotient normalization

proof.text: If $f-g=dh+hd$ with $h$ preserving the filtration, restriction to $F^a$ and passage to $\operatorname{gr}^a$ give the same homotopy equation. On a cycle $x$, $(f-g)x=d(hx)$, so the two maps on cohomology agree, both on the underlying complex and on every step and graded complex. Naturality of the page-one comparison therefore makes $S(f)_1=S(g)_1$. A morphism of spectral sequences satisfies $m_{t+1}=e_VH(m_t)e_U^{-1}$, with $e$ its successor comparison. Induction starting at $t=1$ gives equality on all positive pages. Equality on the image submodules $I_n^a$ and their quotients follows by restriction and quotient of the equal underlying cohomology maps. Hence these assignments are well-defined on the filtered homotopy category.

Let $w:U\to V$ represent an element of $W$. Give $C=\operatorname{Cone}(w)$ the componentwise filtration $F^iC^n=F^iV^n\oplus F^iU^{n+1}$, with differential $(v,u)\mapsto(dv+wu,-du)$. Taking the quotient in each summand gives $\operatorname{gr}^iC=\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{gr}^iw)$ with precisely this differential. The cone criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] makes every such graded complex acyclic. For a fixed $a$, filter $F^aC$ by $G^i=F^{\max(i,a)}C$. Its graded pieces are zero for $i<a$ and $\operatorname{gr}^iC$ for $i\ge a$. The filtration is finite: use common whole and zero bounds of $U,V$, enlarged to include $a$. By [lem-sp-degreewise-filtered-acyclic], $F^aC$ is acyclic. Its displayed differential identifies it with $\operatorname{Cone}(F^aw)$, so the cone criterion gives that every $F^aw$ is a quasi-isomorphism. At a common whole-filtration index this is the underlying map $w$.

source.place: Tag 05S3 (lemma-filtered-derived-functors), cone proof for forget F; Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic); Homology Tag 05QH (lemma-filtered-acyclic)

proof.text: The page-one map of $w$ is $H^{a+b}(\operatorname{gr}^aw)$ under the core comparison, hence bijective. A chain isomorphism of page complexes restricts to an isomorphism on kernels and images and therefore on their cohomology quotients. The successor equation from Step 2 now proves by induction that $S(w)_t$ is bijective at every bidegree for all $t\ge1$. These component inverses commute with the differentials and the successor comparisons, by multiplying the corresponding equations for $S(w)$ by the inverses, so $S(w)$ is an isomorphism of spectral sequences.

source.place: Tags 012M and 012O; induction through successor-page homology

proof.text: For any filtered map $f$, the cohomology square for $F^aU\hookrightarrow U$ and $F^aV\hookrightarrow V$ sends the image submodule $I_n^a(U)$ into $I_n^a(V)$. These restrictions preserve identities and composition. For $w\in W$, both vertical maps in this square are bijective by Step 3. The underlying bijection $H^n(w)$ restricts to a bijection of images: injectivity follows from ambient injectivity, and an element $H^n(\iota_V)y$ in the target image lifts by $y=H^n(F^aw)x$ to $H^n(\iota_U)x$. Thus the inverse preserves every $I_n^a$, and the maps on $I_n^a/I_n^{a+1}$ are also bijective. The filtration is decreasing because the inclusions factor, and finite because whole and zero subcomplex steps give whole and zero cohomology images.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $S$ and to $U\mapsto(H^n(U),I_n)$, with morphisms in the latter target the linear maps preserving every image step. Steps 2, 4 and 5 verify their homotopy invariance and that they invert $W$. This gives the asserted descended functors and their maps on image steps and quotients. Forgetting filtrations also gives a functor $\omega:\mathcal D_f(R)\to D(R)$: filtered homotopies become ordinary homotopies and Step 3 shows that $W$ becomes ordinary quasi-isomorphisms. The cohomology factorization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and uniqueness in the localization universal property identify the descended underlying cohomology functor with $H^n\omega$. Similarly $\operatorname{gr}^a$ gives a functor to $D(R)$, since it takes filtered homotopies to homotopies and $W$ to quasi-isomorphisms by definition. The natural page-one comparison of the core descends by the natural-transformation clause of the same universal property. Its map on a chain representative is exactly $H^{a+b}(\operatorname{gr}^af)$.

Choose bounds $\ell<h$ with $F^\ell U=U$ and $F^hU=0$. Fix $a,n$ and take $t\ge\max(1,h-a,a-\ell+1)$. Then $F^{a+t}U=0$ and $F^{a-t+1}U=U$, as complexes, so $\varphi$ is the actual map $F^aU\to U/F^{a+1}U$. The core image comparison is therefore the first displayed stationary isomorphism. More explicitly, put $C_a=F^aU^n\cap\ker d$, $D_a=F^{a+1}U^n\cap\ker d$, and $B_a=F^aU^n\cap d(U^{n-1})$. The image in $H^n(U/F^{a+1}U)$ is generated by cycles $x\in C_a$, and such a cycle has zero image exactly when $x=dy+z$ for $y\in U^{n-1}$ and $z\in F^{a+1}U^n$. Necessarily $dz=0$ and $dy\in F^aU^n$, so its kernel is $D_a+B_a$. Thus this image is canonically $C_a/(D_a+B_a)$.

source.place: Tag 012K (section-filtered-complex), explicit Z and B formulas; Tag 012W (lemma-biregular-ss-converges), stabilization argument

proof.text: The surjection $C_a\to I_n^a$, $x\mapsto[x]$, has kernel $B_a$. The inverse image of $I_n^{a+1}$ under it is exactly $D_a+B_a$: if $[x]=[z]$ with $z\in D_a$, then $x-z=dy\in B_a$, and the converse is the same equation. Consequently $I_n^a/I_n^{a+1}$ is also $C_a/(D_a+B_a)$. Combining this with Step 7 defines the second displayed isomorphism and its inverse, both on the same representative $x$. This proves precisely the required normalization and its independence of all choices, since the two equivalence relations have just been proved equal.

source.place: Tag 012P (definition-filtration-cohomology-filtered-complex), equations filtration-cohomology and graded-cohomology; omitted intermediate quotient calculation supplied explicitly

proof.text: For a filtered chain map $f:U\to V$, choose $t$ satisfying the bound of Step 7 for both objects. By [lem-kun-filtered-page-functor-normalized], $S$ retains the core image comparison, whose square for $f$ sends the class represented by a cycle $x$ to the class represented by $f(x)$. The normalized stationary map of Step 8 sends those two classes to $[x]$ and $[f(x)]$ modulo the next cohomology image. This proves both stationary comparison squares commute. At adjacent stationary pages $t,t+1$, the subobjects $Z_t,B_t$ are constant by the explicit formulas: cycles are the graded images of $C_a$, and boundaries the graded images of $B_a$. Incoming and outgoing differentials are zero, since their filtration indices lie respectively below $\ell$ and at least $h$. The normalized successor-homology equation supplied by [lem-kun-filtered-page-functor-normalized] sends the class of the graded image of $x\in C_a$ to that same class on page $t+1$. These classes generate the stationary quotient. Hence the two stationary comparisons agree under the successor isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 012M, 012O and 012W; successor quotient normalization applied to stationary cycles

proof.text: Let $\alpha:U\to V$ be a localized morphism. The right-fraction calculus [lem-kun-filtered-quasi-isomorphism-fractions] and the dual of [lem-pc-left-localization-fraction-representation] give a roof $U\xleftarrow{s}T\xrightarrow{f}V$, $s\in W$, with $\alpha=Q(f)Q(s)^{-1}$. Indeed the right-fraction axioms become left-fraction axioms on the opposite category, and a localization remains one on opposites by its universal property. Choose $t'$ at least the given stationary index $t$ for $U,V$ and the bound for $T$. At $t'$ Step 9 proves naturality for $s$ and $f$. The page, cohomology-image and image-quotient maps of $s$ are isomorphisms by Steps 3–5, so multiplying its naturality equation by their inverses gives naturality for $\alpha$. To return from $t'$ to $t$, all intervening pages of $U,V$ are stationary. Their successor comparisons identify the page maps at consecutive indices by the spectral-sequence morphism equation; here taking homology is the identity on the zero-differential page complexes. Step 9 identifies the stationary comparisons at those consecutive indices as well. Descending finitely from $t'$ to $t$ proves the desired square at every index stationary for the two endpoints. It does not require that the roof object already be stationary at $t$. Independence of the roof follows because both maps are the descended functor maps of Step 6.

source.place: Tags 04VE (lemma-morphisms-left-localization) and 04VK (lemma-properties-right-localization), by opposites; Homology Tag 012O and stationary successor comparisons

proof.text: All bounds used above are bounds on filtration indices, common to all degrees of each object. The cone and its step restrictions retain that property, and Step 7 uses no bound on $n$. At $a\ge h$ both stationary sides are zero; at $a<\ell$ one has $I_n^a=I_n^{a+1}=H^n(U)$, again giving zero. The zero complex and the zero ring cause no exception to the cycle and quotient arguments. This completes every clause without imposing any cochain-degree bound.
